title: Instagram Feed: Complete Architecture
description: Design Instagram-scale photo sharing and personalized feed with fan-out-on-write, CDN, and ML ranking.

data.text: Design a photo-sharing social platform like Instagram. Users upload photos and short videos, follow other users, and receive a personalized home feed showing posts from people they follow ranked by relevance. The system must handle 95 million photos uploaded daily, 500 million daily active users viewing their feed, and deliver images with sub-200ms load times globally. Core challenges include feed generation at scale, efficient media delivery, and real-time engagement (likes, comments).

terms.definition: When a user posts, proactively write the post to all followers' feed caches immediately. Fast read, expensive write.
When a user opens the feed, compute it on the fly by querying who they follow. Cheap write, slow read.
Push to feeds of regular users on write; pull for celebrity (10M+ followers) posts on read to avoid write storms.
When a celebrity posts to 10M followers, 10M simultaneous writes overwhelm the fan-out system.
Upload → validation → format conversion → multi-resolution thumbnail generation → CDN distribution.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Upload photos and short videos (Reels up to 90 seconds) with caption and hashtags
Follow/unfollow users; private accounts require follow request approval
Personalized home feed: posts from followed users, ranked by ML model
Like, comment, save, and share posts; see like and comment counts
Stories: 15-second photo/video clips visible for 24 hours
Explore/Discover page: trending posts and recommendations for non-followed accounts
Real-time notifications for likes, comments, follows, mentions
Direct messaging (built on chat system, secondary scope)

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: 95 million photos uploaded per day (~1,100 uploads/s)
Feed load: 500M users × 5 feed opens/day = 2.5B feed requests/day (~29,000 req/s)
Image CDN: serve media with <200ms TTFB from edge
Feed eventual consistency acceptable (lag ≤2s for new posts)
Storage: 95M photos × ~3MB average = ~285 TB/day of raw uploads

data.text: Photo Upload & Hybrid Feed Fan-out Sequence

data.caption: Photo upload, async multi-resolution transcoding, hybrid fan-out to Redis feeds, and ML re-ranking
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Creator as 📸 Creator
    participant Gateway as 🚪 API Gateway
    participant Upload as 📤 Upload Service
    participant S3 as 🗄️ Object Store
    participant Transcode as 🎬 Transcoder / CDN
    participant Kafka as 📨 Kafka Event Bus
    participant Fanout as ⚡ Fanout Worker
    participant Redis as ⚡ Redis Feed Cache
    actor Follower as 👤 Follower
    participant FeedSvc as 📰 Feed Service
    participant ML as 🧠 ML Ranker

    Creator->>Gateway: POST /posts (Image Binary, Caption, Tags)
    Gateway->>Upload: Stream multipart chunks
    Upload->>S3: Store raw image in S3
    Upload->>Transcode: Trigger WebP compression & 3 resolution crops
    Transcode->>S3: Save 240p, 480p, 1080p images
    Upload-->>Creator: Post Created Ack (<500ms)

    Upload->>Kafka: Publish PostCreatedEvent(authorId, postId, timestamp)
    Kafka->>Fanout: Consume event
    Fanout->>Fanout: Check author follower count
    alt Normal Creator (<25,000 Followers)
        Fanout->>Redis: ZADD feed:follower_id timestamp postId (Push to all followers)
    else Celebrity Creator (>25,000 Followers)
        Fanout->>Redis: ZADD user:author_id timestamp postId (Skip fanout push!)
    end

    Follower->>Gateway: GET /feed/home
    Gateway->>FeedSvc: FetchHomeFeed(FollowerId)
    FeedSvc->>Redis: ZREVRANGEBYSCORE feed:follower_id (Top 200 candidates)
    FeedSvc->>Redis: Fetch recent posts from followed celebrities & merge
    FeedSvc->>ML: Score & rank top candidates by engagement signals
    ML-->>FeedSvc: Top 20 Ranked Posts
    FeedSvc-->>Follower: Render Home Feed with CDN images (<150ms)

rows: Write to all N followers' caches
Write to author's post list only
Pull celebrities at load time + merge

items.question: Why hybrid fan-out vs pure push or pure pull?
items.answer: Pure push for a celebrity with 100M followers means 100M Redis writes per post — creating a thundering herd. Pure pull means merging 1000+ followees' timelines on every feed load — too slow. Hybrid pushes for regular users and lazily merges celebrity posts at read time, balancing both.

items.question: How does the ML ranking work on the feed?
items.answer: After fetching the user's pre-built feed cache (last 200 candidates), the ranking model scores each post using signals: relationship strength with author, post recency, predicted engagement (like probability, comment probability, save probability, watch time). Top 20-30 are returned. The model is trained daily on aggregate engagement data.

items.question: How are like counts maintained accurately at 500M DAU scale?
items.answer: Exact counters in SQL become write hotspots. Instagram uses Redis counters with periodic flush to the database. For display, HyperLogLog provides approximate counts (error <1%) at constant memory. For creator analytics, exact counts are computed from the events database asynchronously.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Hybrid fan-out: push posts to normal followers' feed caches; pull celebrity posts at read time
Feed cache per user in Redis (sorted set by timestamp) enables O(log N) inserts and O(1) range reads
CDN with 200+ PoPs is non-negotiable for <200ms image TTFB globally
ML ranking re-scores the top 200 candidates from the feed cache, not the entire post graph
Image pipeline: original → multi-resolution WebP variants → CDN, deduplicated by hash
data.takeaway: Instagram-scale feed generation requires separating the write path (fan-out to Redis caches) from the read path (cache reads + ML re-ranking), with CDN handling the enormous media delivery load.
